notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Kickoff with Dr. Elaine Voss and Tomas Reyes. Consolidating three legacy EHRs (acquired hospitals) onto one platform. $6.1M engagement. Executive team wants all 5 hospitals live on the same date for simplicity.

notes.author: Leo Brandt
notes.text: Data profiling: medication allergy codes use 3 different vocabularies; 9% of allergy records failed automated mapping. Patient-safety risk if migrated all at once without clinical validation.

notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Proposed facility-by-facility rollout starting with the smallest hospital, with clinician champions per unit and a clinical data validation sign-off before each go-live. Dr. Voss backed it; Tomas worried about longer dual licensing costs (~$900k).

notes.author: Leo Brandt
notes.text: First hospital live. Champions handled most workflow questions at the elbow. Two order-set issues found and fixed centrally before the next facility.

notes.author: Leo Brandt
notes.text: Hospitals 2 and 3 live. Allergy mapping error rate down to 0.4% after clinicians validated the mapping tables. Abby Chen: "The champions made nurses feel heard, not steamrolled."

notes.author: Mira Castellanos
notes.text: Remaining hospitals live. Dual licensing cost overran by ~15% but no reportable patient-safety events linked to the migration. Board satisfied.

notes.author: Leo Brandt
notes.text: Hypercare complete. Recommend documenting the champion model and validation gate for the firm.

simulation.lesson: When consolidating several legacy record systems where data errors carry safety or compliance risk, a site-by-site rollout with frontline champions and a formal data-validation sign-off before each go-live outperforms a simultaneous launch. The extra cost of running old and new systems in parallel for longer is real but is usually smaller than the cost of a data-quality failure at scale.
simulation.why: Domain experts validating mapped data per wave catches errors automation misses; champions drive adoption.
simulation.conditions: Heterogeneous legacy data, high consequence of data errors, frontline user adoption risk.
